summary: Improve MHPSS coordination, supervision, referrals, and quality monitoring. Explore the course outline and practical learning outcomes.
lede: Coordinated psychosocial support connects community wellbeing activities with appropriate mental health care. For coordinators, community practitioners and supervisors, this course develops practical ways to map service roles, plan safeguarded group activities and strengthen referrals. You will also work with supervision checklists, consent-aware information handling, participant feedback and monitoring measures to improve service quality while respecting non-specialist role boundaries.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits practitioners who coordinate, deliver, supervise, or monitor community-based psychosocial support and need to improve the links between activities, referral services, and quality checks.
modules: IASC MHPSS Pyramid in Service Design
WHO Psychological First Aid in Practice
prerequisites: Working familiarity with community services, psychosocial support, health, education, or protection work is expected. Clinical diagnosis or treatment experience is not required; the course focuses on service coordination, safe support activities, supervision, and referral practice.
